reason: The cited lines show the tool validates parameters, sends a fixed socket message named "browser_click", then retrieves and returns the browser URL, title, and accessibility snapshot. They do not show arbitrary host code execution. They also do not show agent-supplied data being sent to an attacker-readable destination; the socket message is to a fixed browser/control channel. The returned URL/title/snapshot may contain non-public or attacker-controlled page content depending on what the browser is viewing, but these lines alone do not establish that the content is secret or attacker-controlled.
